Title: Diagnosis of test `testGetStringInconsistentRecord`

Details: The test `testGetStringInconsistentRecord` expects an `IllegalArgumentException` when trying to get the value by the header name "fourth" from the record `recordWithHeader`. In the test, the key "fourth" is added to `header` with value 4, then `recordWithHeader.get("fourth")` is called.

The method `CSVRecord.get(String name)` first checks if `mapping` (the header map) is `null`, throwing an IllegalStateException if it is. Otherwise, it looks up the index for the given name from `mapping`. If the name is not found (`index == null`), it returns null. If found, it returns the value at that index from `values`.

From the constructor, `CSVRecord` is constructed with a `mapping` (header map) and an array of `values`. The `mapping` is a `Map<String, Integer>` associating header names to their indexes into `values`.

The test adds "fourth" with index 4 to the `header` map, but `recordWithHeader` apparently does not have "fourth" in its `mapping`, or the values array does not have an element at index 4, or the header map given to `recordWithHeader` is inconsistent with the `header` map. This inconsistent state leads to `recordWithHeader.get("fourth")` not throwing `IllegalArgumentException` as expected, but instead returning null or throwing some other exception.

The root cause is that the record's internal mapping and values do not match the updated header map in the test, so the test assumes an exception will be thrown when accessing a missing header, but the actual method returns null instead if the header name is missing from the record's `mapping`.

Hence, the failure is because `CSVRecord.get(String)` does not throw `IllegalArgumentException` when the requested header is not in the record's own mapping; it returns null instead. This is inconsistent with test expectations.

The class and method to fix is likely `CSVRecord.get(String)` to throw `IllegalArgumentException` when the requested name is not found in the mapping rather than returning null.

Suggested fix locations:
org.apache.commons.csv.CSVRecord.get(java.lang.String)
